biography.plain_text: Eric De Vocht is a Belgian architect and property developer behind IRET's office and retail projects. Raised in Schoten, he learnt about building sites from his father, architect Maurice De Vocht. He became a major private investor in commercial developments across Belgium, including the Rive Gauche shopping centre in Charleroi.

confidence.reason: Official business material and broadcaster reporting corroborate the career; the paternal and upbringing particulars rely on specialist Belgian business reporting.

long_biography.plain_text:
Eric De Vocht and his wife, Maryse Odeurs, converted a former monastery and hospital into Botanic Sanctuary Antwerp. Their company IRET took a long lease on the historic site, commissioned research into its buildings and organised the restoration. The old chapel became a venue for concerts and ceremonies, while the former infirmary was adapted for events.

De Vocht's property work has also involved prolonged assembly of urban sites. In Cannes, he pursued the 33 Croisette development over more than three decades, working with estate agent Michaël Zingraf from the first apartment purchase. The plans combined apartments with shops on the seafront.

confidence.reason: Official hotel history and the architects' account support the conversion; a named project participant's interview supports the Cannes history.
